cards.title: Direct HTTP Dispatch For Zero-Tool Seats
cards.body: Host subagents incur massive startup overhead by loading system instructions, git status, and environment context on every spawn. In measured runs, rank ballots consumed roughly 64,000 tokens each for a tiny 2,000-token prompt packet, totaling 193,000 tokens across voters. Yet the dispatch logic already classifies vote, rank, control, and elder phases as requiring zero tools. The dispatcher should execute zero-tool seats directly via lightweight HTTP completions whenever provider credentials exist, bypassing full subagent instantiation. This single architectural shift eliminates over 80 percent of ballot and elder token consumption while slashing loop latency without compromising isolation or protocol invariants.
cards.evidence: docs/council-run-2026-11-13-self-review.md (rank vote 193k tokens across 3 ballots, ~64k each); src/run/dispatch.rs (tools_for marks vote, rank, elders, control as 'none')
cards.eli5: Route zero-tool seats through fast HTTP completions instead of spawning heavy subagents with tens of thousands of startup tokens.

cards.title: Minimalist Dynamic MCP Toolset Gating
cards.body: The MCP server currently advertises between 22 and 27 tools on tools/list, outputting 19 to 23 kilobytes of comprehensive JSON schemas. When an AI host initializes or interacts with the server, these exhaustive schemas are injected directly into context, consuming several thousand prompt tokens on every turn. The server should default to a compact core toolset containing only primary workflow operations such as init, next, ingest, status, cut, and note. Specialized administrative tools like blind verification, memory reconfiguration, and lock inspection should remain tucked behind an explicit flag or progressive disclosure. This reduces baseline MCP token consumption without removing any functionality.
cards.evidence: src/mcp.rs (tools_list sends 19 KB to 23 KB across 22 to 27 tool schemas); src/api.rs (registry defines toolset groupings)
cards.eli5: Default MCP tools list to a compact six-tool core, cutting massive schema bloat on every host prompt.
